items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: I remember -- I don't know whether it was Tulsa, Oklahoma City where they had a dance contest, where I can't remember how he spelled his name, but it was one that stuck out in my mind; his name was Jack Wiggins.

ctx.x: For instance, in Florida, I know we would play Tampa for three days and Pensacola for three days and that type of thing, but it would be in theatres -- and the theatres would always be packed. We'd play Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Oklahoma, and many of the really, the -- as I say, Bessie Smith was on TOBA, Mamie Smith was on TOBA -- and that was when I really learned to dance.

Because they used to have really great dances, and I remember -- I don't know whether it was Tulsa, Oklahoma City where they had a dance contest, where I can't remember how he spelled his name, but it was one that stuck out in my mind; his name was Jack Wiggins. Jack Wiggins was really a great dancer, and they had others that thought that they were great -- all of them thought that they were the greatest!
